findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is `isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`. A user must be both admin and owner, and for team bookings the owner may not count as admin, so legitimate admins and owners are denied. For bookings without a team, `teamId ?? 0` is also queried with a bogus id. It should be `||`.

findings.title: Any attendee can add guests, and email match is case-sensitive
findings.body: Any existing attendee (matched by `user.email`) is allowed to add guests to the booking, and attendees can be arbitrary people who booked. This lets an attendee make Cal.com send emails and calendar invites to arbitrary addresses. Combined with the emails going out under the organizer's name, it is an abuse vector. The comparison is also case-sensitive, so it can reject legitimate matches.

findings.title: Dedup and blacklist comparisons are case-sensitive and ignore duplicate inputs
findings.body: Blacklisted emails are lowercased, but `guest` is compared as-is, so `Foo@X.com` bypasses the blacklist. Comparison with existing attendees is also case-sensitive, so the same address with different casing is added twice. Duplicates within the `guests` input are not removed server-side, because the uniqueness check exists only in client code. This can cause duplicate attendee rows.

findings.title: Emails use the unfiltered `guests` list rather than the guests actually added
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` receives the raw input, not `uniqueGuests`. Blacklisted or already-existing emails are therefore treated as 'new guests'. They receive the scheduled-invitation email instead of the add-guests notification, and blacklisted addresses still get mail. Pass `uniqueGuests`.

findings.title: Calendar update is not error-handled after the DB write
findings.body: Attendees are committed to the DB before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees`. If that call throws, the mutation returns an error while the guests are already saved, and no emails are sent. Retrying then fails with 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' because the guests already exist. There is no transaction or compensation. The `catch` around the email send only does `console.log` and discards the error.

findings.title: Credentials and EventManager use the acting user, not the organizer
findings.body: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({...user})` use the logged-in user's credentials. When an attendee or team admin adds guests, the calendar event owned by the organizer is updated with the wrong user's credentials. The update can fail or silently do nothing. The booking's organizer credentials (already included in the query) should be used.

findings.title: New guests take the organizer's locale and timezone
findings.body: Guests are created with the organizer's `timeZone` and `locale`, so guest emails and times are rendered in the organizer's locale and timezone rather than the guest's. New guests also have an empty name.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores disable-email settings and sends wrong mails to existing attendees
findings.body: Unlike the sibling functions, it takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and does not check `disableStandardEmails`. Hosts and attendees who opted out still get emails. Organizer emails are also sent unconditionally. Because the `evt.attendees` list comes from the updated booking, every attendee is covered; the 'else' branch correctly uses AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but only for those not in the raw input (see the unfiltered `guests` issue).

findings.title: Error toast shows 'CODE: message' and the fallback is unreachable
findings.body: `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`` is always a non-empty string, so `|| t("unable_to_add_guests")` never triggers. Users see messages like 'BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid' prefixed with a raw error code. Also, `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` is recreated on every render inside the component.

findings.title: Empty-string entries and stale error state are not handled
findings.body: The initial value is `[""]`, and `handleAdd` only checks `length === 0`. The empty email is caught only through the zod validation error, so the error message is misleading. `isInvalidEmail` is never reset on a successful add, on a subsequent edit, or when the dialog closes via the overlay, so the error persists the next time the dialog is opened.

findings.title: Add-guests action is shown for every booking in the edit menu, including seated events
findings.body: The 'additional_guests' action is added unconditionally to `editBookingActions`. Its id is 'add_members', which is misleading. It is not restricted to bookings the user may modify (for example, attendee-only views). Seated events are not handled and would get a mix of seat references.
